title: Added locally generated Text-To-Speech to my game using Overtone
author: LandoRingel

comments.author: MysteriousPepper8908
comments.body: What are the hardware requirements? Seems like running a game and a local LLM simultaneously would be demanding.

replies.author: LandoRingel
replies.body: It will run on a standard 1080

replies.author: MysteriousPepper8908
replies.body: Really? Interesting, must be a very lightweight model as there's clearly some actual language processing going on here and not just TTS.

comments.author: Thistlemanizzle
comments.body:
This is genuinely impressive. Local is always going to get beaten out by cloud, but for local this is usable.

Is the video sped up in any way? The lag between call and response is really small, it’s not a long wait at all.

replies.author: LandoRingel
replies.body: I sped up the parts where I'm typing! The AI replies much faster than I can type XD

comments.author: dragonboltz
comments.body: This is really cool! I love seeing folks experiment with locally generated TTS in games. How hard was it to hook Overtone into your dialogue system? Can you tweak the voice characteristics easily, or is it pretty fixed? I'm curious about the perfomrance impact too.

comments.author: cs_cast_away_boi
comments.body: You’re at the forefront of games! Now you just need to figure out how to create a system that turns the speech into actions in the games lol

comments.author: smellysocks234
comments.body: Interesting as an MVP but I would hate to have in a game I'm playing. The voice isn't good enough yet.

comments.author: Euchale
comments.body: I hope you are still working on getting emotion in that voice. I know its really though with the TTS models available at the moment.
